reason: The 288-byte scratch stride is a small, distinct layout change, but cache benefit is unknown and the 272-byte variant was not promoted. The tiled NEON transpose could reduce conversion cost in the previously measured TB path, though TB lost and its conversion cost was not isolated. Four-step and K-pair unrolling have uncertain benefit and risk code growth or register pressure; the K-pair proposal may overlap prior unrolling. Half-band packing adds work and resembles an unpromoted traversal. TA adds a timed B transpose while retaining both generated packing paths. Fusion repeats the A transpose across 16 column panels, producing 16 MiB of transposed values instead of 1 MiB in the full-buffer path, so its cost risk is highest. These are evidence-based priorities, not predicted gains.
